groups.title: VNC expansion boundary
groups.writingJob: Distinguish the directional inside the VNC from antecessive and negative particles outside it.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader see which modifiers belong to the VNC and which modify it from outside.
groups.decisionSplit: The later controls supply genuine modifier choices; the application preserves their different boundaries.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add one generic expansion control; use the real directional, antecessive, and polarity choices.
groups.derivedCueJob: Mark each modifier as VNC-internal or VNC-external.
groups.proposal: Keep the three Lesson 8 modifier systems separate at the VNC boundary.

groups.title: Direction and location
groups.writingJob: Place on or huāl in its licensed VNC-internal position, apply its boundary effects, and preserve its directional or locative contribution.
groups.readingJob: Guide literal, nonliteral, locative, bidirectional, and context-dependent readings of on and huāl.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses no directional, on, or huāl and may choose the rare licensed on plus itt-a contraction; the application performs placement and spelling.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the directional picker and the typed rare-contraction choice; do not expose carrier spelling or slot order.
groups.derivedCueJob: Show the directional's grammatical job, position, meaning, and automatic boundary changes.
groups.proposal: Make direction a genuine choice while keeping its realization and interpretation Canvas-governed.

groups.title: Earlier-event ō
groups.writingJob: Allow optional ō outside a compatible past-tense VNC, block incompatible uses, and preserve its earlier-event scope.
groups.readingJob: Explain the completed or earlier-event reading without reducing ō to the English word already.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses whether to use ō when available; the application decides availability, position, and scope.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the antecessive checkbox and hide or block it when the selected grammar does not license it.
groups.derivedCueJob: Show ō as an external earlier-event modifier and identify its scope.
groups.proposal: Keep antecessive ō optional, past-sensitive, VNC-external, and meaning-bearing.

groups.title: Negative ah and ca scope
groups.writingJob: Place the selected negative outside the VNC or its fore-lying modifier group and enforce ca's trigger conditions.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through negative scope when English word order hides it.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses polarity; the application selects the licensed negative structure and its attachment.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse polarity and particle choices; do not expose raw negative-prefix placement.
groups.proposal: Make negative scope grammatical rather than a printed-string choice.

groups.title: Sentence and transformation
groups.writingJob: Turn a selected grammatical clause into a written sentence with the proper transformation and final punctuation.
groups.readingJob: Distinguish basic sentences from single-base and double-base transformations.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended sentence use; the application derives capitalization, punctuation, and compatible transformations.
groups.controlPolicy: Use genuine sentence choices only; do not ask for abstract transformation labels.
groups.proposal: Treat sentence form as a grammatical projection of the selected clause and intent.

groups.title: Affirmative assertion
groups.writingJob: Build a simple affirmative assertion from an indicative nuclear clause with optional outside modifiers.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader from the complete sentence back to its clause and modifiers.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a statement; the application enforces the indicative-clause requirement.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse sentence type, mood, and particles without a duplicate affirmative control.
groups.proposal: Make the basic statement the unchanged sentence use of a licensed indicative clause.

groups.title: Negative assertion
groups.writingJob: Convert an affirmative assertion into its licensed negative sentence while preserving particle scope.
groups.readingJob: Guide different negative readings without treating every negative-looking particle as the same operation.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses negative polarity; the application composes it with the selected particles and clause.
groups.proposal: Build negative assertions through one scope-aware sentence path.

groups.title: Emphatic assertion
groups.writingJob: Add emphatic ca to an affirmative or negative assertion in its licensed position.
groups.readingJob: Guide the emphatic force separately from clause introduction and polarity.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses emphasis; the application orders ca with the negative element and clause.
groups.controlPolicy: Use the particle combination system rather than a duplicate sentence-type value.
groups.proposal: Make emphasis a particle choice composed with polarity and statement structure.

groups.title: Yes-no question by intonation
groups.writingJob: Turn a statement into a yes-no question by sentence use and question-mark realization.
groups.readingJob: Recognize a yes-no question even when no interrogative particle is present.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses question; the application supplies question punctuation and preserves the clause grammar.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse sentence type; do not add an intonation spelling field.
groups.proposal: Make the punctuation change the written projection of a genuine question choice.

groups.title: Yes-no question with cuix
groups.writingJob: Build a yes-no question with cuix outside the nuclear clause and preserve licensed interpretations.
groups.readingJob: Guide the question and the context-dependent readings of the verbstem without confusing them with cuix itself.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a cuix question; the application orders the particle and punctuation.
groups.controlPolicy: Use the particle picker together with sentence type; do not duplicate cuix in a question-mode control.
groups.proposal: Compose cuix with the same canonical question and sentence path.
